patterns_data.what_is_impacting: TX / VA / OH / KY authorization status and facility classification
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with MCC

patterns_data.pattern_details: A large share of apparent spend growth is tied to authorization classification movement and unmapped facility assignment rather than a clearly confirmed utilization trend. TX authorization-code redistribution is the largest issue, and additional dollars sit in Not Mapped facility buckets in TX, OH, and KY, with a smaller but still material validation signal in VA. Validate PA-to-claim mapping and facility assignment before tightening UM rules or changing reimbursement, because part of the increase may be administrative drift instead of true medical change.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is a high-dollar gating issue that can misdirect utilization, reimbursement, and network actions if left unresolved.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM, reimbursement, and data-quality reconciliation of PA status mapping and facility-type assignment in TX first, then VA, OH, and KY; only after that should business teams apply policy or contracting changes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: These groups are explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shift and include unmapped facility values, so business action should wait for data confirmation.
evidence_summary: TX AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION accounts for about +$65.2M of the apparent increase and is flagged for validation before action.
TX DSNP HMO claims in Not Mapped facilities added about +$9.1M, with 225 more admissions and about +$24.0K higher paid per admit.
VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION adds about +$0.7M tied to Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with MCC.
OH and KY Not Mapped Medicare or DSNP HMO segments add about +$0.6M more and are also flagged as unmapped.

patterns_data.top_pattern: TX special needs products are driving a major acute hospital admission surge
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: TX / ACUTE HOSPITAL / DSNP HMO and CSNP HMO
patterns_data.pattern_details: TX special needs products are seeing a very large rise in authorized acute hospital spend driven mainly by more inpatient activity, not higher price per admission. DSNP HMO contributes most of the increase, and CSNP HMO adds a smaller but still material lift. This is an inpatient volume-management issue first, with thousands of added admissions despite slightly lower paid per admit.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest confirmed utilization-led pattern and can outweigh savings from smaller reimbursement or coding actions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a TX SNP inpatient action plan focused on admission appropriateness, avoidable readmissions, discharge planning, and repeat high-use members in acute hospitals.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased about +$74.1M on 3,589 more admissions and 4,194 more claims.
TX CSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased about +$9.6M on 437 more admissions and 540 more claims.
In both products, paid per admit fell slightly, pointing to admission growth rather than pricing as the main driver.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Atrial fibrillation ablation episodes are expanding in Medicare HMO acute hospitals
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: OH / IN / NY / Medicare HMO / ACUTE HOSPITAL cardiac rhythm procedures
key_driver_codes: Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation
patterns_data.pattern_details: A focused cardiac rhythm management pattern is expanding in Medicare HMO acute hospitals, led by concomitant left atrial appendage closure and cardiac ablation episodes. OH is the largest market and shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit, while similar smaller emergence appears in IN and NY. This looks like targeted case-mix expansion rather than broad inpatient inflation, and it includes some provider concentration at ADVOCATE SOUTH SUBURBAN HOSPITAL.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Focused procedure growth can create outsized cost pressure quickly and often responds better to targeted clinical and UM review than broad medical policy changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send these episodes to clinical and UM teams for procedure-level appropriateness review, coding consistency checks, and provider concentration analysis, starting with OH and then IN and NY.
evidence_summary: OH atrial fibrillation cases tied to Concomitant Left Atrial Appendage Closure and Cardiac Ablation added about +$5.2M, including 94 more admissions across two AF diagnoses.
OH Medicare HMO acute hospital spend for the same procedure added about +$3.1M on 61 more admissions with about +$8.0K higher paid per admit.
IN added about +$1.3M and NY about +$1.2M for the same procedure, showing the pattern is spreading beyond OH.
ADVOCATE SOUTH SUBURBAN HOSPITAL appears in both OH and IN as a smaller but recurring concentration point.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Within TX DSNP HMO acute hospital growth, a concentrated set of digestive complication and blood disorder episodes is adding both volume and cost intensity. Red blood cell disorder admissions, including sickle cell crisis and anemia-related cases, and digestive MCC admissions, including post-procedural complications and gastrostomy malfunction, are the key drivers. This is a focused clinical management issue inside the broader TX inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated clinical mix allows targeted intervention on recurrent admissions, complications, and care pathways instead of broad hospital-wide action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and UM teams review these TX DSNP episodes for recurrent admission drivers, complication prevention opportunities, and case-management interventions for sickle cell, anemia, and post-procedural digestive cases.
evidence_summary: TX HB-SS DISEASE WITH CRISIS UNS under Red Blood Cell Disorders without MCC added about +$1.2M on 96 more admissions.
TX DSNP HMO Red Blood Cell Disorders without MCC added another +$0.8M on 42 more admissions with about +$3.1K higher paid per admit.
Other Digestive System Diagnoses with MCC contributed about +$1.0M combined across post-procedural digestive complications and gastrostomy malfunction.
ACUTE POSTHEMORRHAGIC ANEMIA added about +$0.4M with about +$6.6K higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CHRIST HOSPITAL is showing unit-cost pressure across multiple OH products
patterns_data.pattern_details: At CHRIST HOSPITAL, acute hospital spend is rising even as admissions decline across three products, indicating reimbursement or billing intensity pressure rather than demand growth. Medicare HMO is the largest contributor, with similar unit-cost patterns in PPO Regional and DSNP HMO. This is a provider economics issue, not a broad utilization wave.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When cost rises despite lower volume, contracting, payment terms, or billing intensity become the main business levers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a provider-level reimbursement review for CHRIST HOSPITAL covering contract terms, case-rate changes, and outlier billing patterns across Medicare HMO, PPO Regional, and DSNP HMO.
evidence_summary: OH Medicare HMO at CHRIST HOSPITAL added about +$1.1M even with 50 fewer admissions, while paid per admit rose about +$3.7K.
OH PPO Regional added about +$0.3M with 2 fewer admissions and about +$14.8K higher paid per admit.
OH DSNP HMO added about +$0.2M with 15 fewer admissions and about +$2.7K higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic and transplant-related cases need individual case management, not broad policy changes
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IN / TX / UNATTRIBUTED / VA / OH rare high-cost inpatient cases
key_driver_codes: ENC AFTERCARE FLW MX ORGN TRANSPL
Coronary Bypass without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC
Amputation for Circulatory System Disorders Except Upper Limb and Toe with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: This pattern is made up of one-off or very rare high-cost inpatient cases, including transplant aftercare, major cardiothoracic surgery, coronary bypass, amputation, and other severe episodes. Counts are very small, but the cost per case is high enough to create noticeable spend movement. These are best handled through individual case validation and large-case management, not through broad utilization policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rare outliers can distort trend signals and require stop-loss, case-management, and claim-validation responses instead of program-wide intervention.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route these cases to clinical review and large-case management for claim-level validation, severity confirmation, and any applicable stop-loss or transplant case management follow-up.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is built from very small counts and low-baseline cases, so claim-level confirmation is needed before drawing broader conclusions.
evidence_summary: A single lung transplant aftercare admission added about +$0.4M.
Multi-organ transplant aftercare added about +$0.1M, and an aortic dissection case added about +$0.1M.
OH rare one-case episodes included about +$46K for coronary bypass and about +$45K for amputation related to diabetic gangrene.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the main TX and OH drivers, a dispersed set of smaller authorization-related increases is appearing across acute hospital, physical rehab, and long-term care settings. The pattern recurs across Medicare HMO, DSNP HMO, CSNP HMO, and PPO Local products, usually in digestive, red blood cell, or aftercare DRGs. Each local pocket is small, but together they add up and should be managed through targeted market-level UM and provider review rather than enterprise-wide changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: These smaller pockets can quietly accumulate into meaningful spend if they are ignored because each local segment looks small on its own.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Assign these smaller segments to local UM and network teams for market-by-market review, prioritizing repeat authorized admissions, provider mix shifts, and post-acute routing before launching enterprise rule changes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Many contributing groups are low-baseline or small-volume, so targeted case-level confirmation is needed before scaling actions broadly.
evidence_summary: AZ / CA / CT / MO / TX / VA Medicare HMO acute hospital mixed pressure added about +$1.4M.
CT / VA DSNP HMO acute hospital utilization added about +$1.1M, largely from VA red blood cell and digestive admissions.
FL / IN / NJ / NY / OH DSNP HMO acute hospital mixed pressure added about +$0.9M, led by NJ and NY Red Blood Cell Disorders without MCC.
Smaller KY, OH, AZ, CT, and IN pockets across PPO Local, Physical Rehab, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, and Acute Hospital added about +$0.8M more, many with low-baseline volume.
